 pending in the Court of the learned Addl. District and Sessions  Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Angul.
2. The petitioner had approached the learned Addl. District and  Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Angul in  Special (POCSO) Case No. 60 of 2025 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 01.12.2025 rejected  the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the  petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 483 of  Page 1 of 4  BNSS, 2023 praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.

1 at 01.50 PM, the complainant aged about 28 years of village Sankhamur appeared at PS and presented a written report that one Sachin Kumar Sahoo of her village has kept illicit relationship with her several times since 14 years by giving false assurance to marry her.
When he did not marry her, she had married to another person before 05 years.
After 05 days of her marriage, she has left her father-in-law's house as because he told her that if she will not return, he will die.
Basing on such version, she returned back to her parents' house.
Then he has been keeping physical relation with her many times by giving false assurance to marry her.

When she is insisted him to marry her,
he is threatening her to publish her nude photos in social medias.
Further he has taken a sum of Rs 1,20,000/- from her by giving threatening to publish her photos.
On 25.08.2025, he called her to his house for discussion on marriage.
Accordingly, she had been to his house and he kept physical relation with her.
When she demanded to marry him, he threatened to publish her nude photos.
He along with his mother assaulted her and threatened her against dire consequences.
Hence, the FIR.

5. Although during investigation the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
where she has very specifically alleged against the petitioner, however when she appeared in the witness box, she has wriggled out of her earlier statement.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the cross examination part of the evidence of the victim girl which reads as under:-
"8.
I cannot say who scribed the FIR.
I only put my signature on the FIR.
I cannot say the contents of the FIR.
9. I was not examined by the police.
As per the instruction of police, I signed on the blank printed form.
I cannot say the contents of the documents.
10. I cannot say the contents of the statement recorded by the Magistrate.
As per the instruction of police, I gave my statement before the Magistrate.
11. Police obtained my signature on some documents.

12. I want to marry with the accused Sachin Kumar Sahu."
7.
The petitioner is in custody since 31.08.2025.
Notice was issued to the informant on 18.12.2025.

Pursuant thereto, Mr. Pratap Kumar Nayak, learned counsel entered appearance on behalf of the informant and submits that he does not have any objection if bail is granted to the petitioner.
8.
Regard being had to the nature of allegation against petitioner and his period of custody since 31.08.2025, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

9. Hence, the Petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:

sentences.text: (1) The petitioner shall appear before the Court diligently without fail, on every date of hearing; and default in appearance before the trial court even for once will entail withdrawal of the concession of bail granted by this Court;
(2) He shall not influence any of the witnesses related to this case in any manner whatsoever; and (3) He shall not commit any offence while on bail.
(4) He shall be released on bail subject to verification of similar type of antecedents.

In the event, the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
10. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
